title: Importing Multi-Tab Excel Files into Business Central
summary: This post explains how to import multi-tab Excel files into Business Central with a header/line relationship structure. It provides code examples using AL to read separate header and line sheets, maintain relational integrity with a dictionary-based key mapping system, and populate staging tables.

title: Happy Thanksgiving 2025
summary: A brief holiday greeting with no Business Central technical content or features discussed.

title: Importing XML into Business Central with AL
summary: The post demonstrates how to parse cXML (commerce eXtensible Markup Language) files in Business Central using AL code without specialized XML codeunits. It walks through a practical example of extracting purchase order data from an XML file and populating custom tables, highlighting the hierarchical node-based navigation required for XML parsing.

title: Managing Optional Extensions in Business Central AL Code
summary: This post explains how to create a single Business Central extension that optionally interacts with a third-party extension without creating a hard dependency. The technique uses NavApp.GetModuleInfo to detect if an optional extension is installed, then uses RecordRef and FieldRef to conditionally set extension-specific fields.

title: Debugging Business Event Subscriptions in Business Central
summary: Business Central has hidden pages for debugging Business Event Subscriptions (which function as web hooks). To resolve subscription issues, verify permissions, check the Business Event Activity Log to see notification delivery attempts and retries, and review the Business Event Notifications page to confirm events were sent.

title: 2025 Highlights: Engaging Moments in Business Central Events
summary: A community contributor reflects on 2025 engagements across Business Central events, podcasts, and a growing technical blog covering AL Development, sharing key topics like AI, workflows, and open source tools with the community.

title: Integrating Analysis Views in Business Central Extensions
summary: Business Central AL 17.0 Runtime adds the ability to package and deploy Analysis Views in extensions. You can export Analysis View definitions as JSON files, include them in page or page extension AL code, and deploy them to automatically add pre-built analysis views to list pages in any Business Central environment.

title: Streamline Your AL Development with Global NuGet Symbols
summary: Business Central AL 17.0 allows developers to download Business Central symbols from Global NuGet feeds instead of needing a live client environment or copying symbols from other projects. This streamlines AL extension development by adding al.symbolsCountryRegion configuration and using a new download symbols command in Visual Studio Code.

title: How to Use External APIs in Business Central
summary: This post explains how to consume external APIs from within Business Central by making HTTP requests using the HttpClient data type and parsing JSON responses. It includes two practical examples: retrieving Chuck Norris jokes and validating email addresses through public APIs, with complete AL code samples and guidance on security prompts.

title: Step-by-Step Guide to AI Campaigns in Business Central
summary: A practical guide to building AI-powered marketing campaigns in Business Central using two coordinated AI agents. The system generates regional postal codes based on natural language prompts and automatically adds free samples to sales orders shipping to targeted regions, minimizing AI costs by preprocessing data rather than running AI logic on every transaction.

title: Using AI to Simplify Complex Documentation and Design Tasks
summary: A developer describes using Microsoft 365 Copilot with Notebooks to parse supplier requirements documents and map them to Business Central AL development tasks, including header and line field definitions, improving efficiency in understanding complex API and file export formats.

title: Getting Started with AI for Rapid Software Development for Business Central
summary: This post demonstrates using Copilot Chat and other AI tools to accelerate Business Central software development by extracting functional requirements from unstructured sources like meeting transcripts, then designing a real-world accounting system for a space travel agency that tracks asset depreciation by time and usage events, manages launch-based mission costing, and integrates with Business Central for GL posting.

title: How Copilot and AI Inspired My Card Game Design
summary: A developer used Copilot to design a card game combining image generation prompts with competitive gameplay mechanics. The post demonstrates how Copilot can assist in creative learning, from initial concept through final game production.

title: Step-by-Step Guide: Create Agents in AL Code
summary: Building agents in Business Central AL involves creating setup tables, pages, codeunits, and enums to enable autonomous multi-step operations. The guide walks through creating a Cash Flow Review Agent that can accept tasks, interact with the user during execution, and display KPI results.

title: Join the First Business Central Hackathon at DynamicsCon 2026
summary: The first Business Central Hackathon is being hosted at DynamicsCon 2026 on May 13th as an evening creative sprint where teams build AI-related solutions. The event welcomes developers of all skill levels, low-code creators, and professionals to collaborate, experiment, and learn through hands-on building in a social, low-pressure environment focused on Business Central and AI.

title: Leveraging RecordRef and FieldRef for Dynamic Coding
summary: This post explains how to use weakly typed RecordRef and FieldRef objects in Business Central AL for dynamic, flexible code when you don't know the record type at compile time. It contrasts weakly typed objects with strongly typed ones and demonstrates practical use cases like summing amounts across different table types and exporting any record set to Excel.

title: Understanding Dimension Set Id in AL for Business Central
summary: Dimension Set ID is a Business Central concept that deduplicates dimension combinations to reduce data storage. The post explains why dimensions are superior to segment-based accounting and provides AL code to retrieve or create a Dimension Set ID by building temporary dimension entries and passing them to the DimensionManagement codeunit.

title: Streamline AL Development Using Copilot Code Review
summary: GitHub's Copilot Code Review feature can assist with AL code reviews by checking code against detailed standards beyond what CI pipelines catch. Set up the feature in GitHub settings and create a codereview.instructions.md file with AL-specific guidelines to guide Copilot's review process and ensure AppSource-ready, high-quality extensions.

title: The Unbounded Growth Equation: Why AI Works Best When You Keep (and Grow) Your Team
summary: AI succeeds as a force multiplier that amplifies existing teams rather than replacing them. While cost-cutting has inherent limits, AI enables unlimited productivity gains when humans stay in control to steer, correct, and imagine alongside AI tools.

title: Navigating Namespace Changes in Business Central 28
summary: Business Central 28 introduces fully qualified names for pages, codeunits, reports, and record references, allowing developers to reference objects directly without requiring using statements at the top of files. This improves code clarity by making object origins explicit at the point of use.

title: Overcoming Integer Limits in Business Central with BigInteger
summary: Business Central's integer data type maxes out at 2.1 billion records, a limit some implementations have hit. AL Version 18 (Business Central 2026 Wave 1) now supports migrating integer fields to BigInteger, which extends the range to 9.2 quintillion values, with compiler warnings to prevent overflow issues.

title: Effective Steps for Troubleshooting Business Central Agents
summary: This post explains how to troubleshoot Business Central agents by examining task logs, step-by-step operations, and detailed agent actions. It covers analyzing agent reasoning, reviewing data visibility, adjusting agent permissions and profiles, and monitoring Copilot credit consumption.

title: Step-by-Step Guide to Secure Business Central Agent Implementations in AL
summary: This post demonstrates how to secure AI agents in Business Central by implementing restrictive profiles, page customizations, and permission sets. It shows the security risks of overly permissive agent configurations and provides step-by-step AL code examples to limit what agents can see and do.

title: My 2026 Tradeshow Schedule and Highlights
summary: A presenter outlines their 2026 tradeshow schedule at Directions and DynamicsCon, featuring sessions on AI-powered Business Central extensions, performance optimization with telemetry tools, deprecation of OData page endpoints, and hackathon preparation, with code examples and resources to be shared after the events.

title: Native SFTP Support in Business Central 28
summary: Native SFTP support was briefly introduced in Business Central 28 via a new SFTP Client codeunit, enabling asynchronous file operations with external servers. However, Microsoft removed this feature due to security hardening concerns, requiring users to use Azure Functions as an alternative for SFTP connectivity.

title: Maximizing Productivity with Copilot Cowork Skills
summary: Copilot Cowork Skills enable repeatable, structured AI workflows that go beyond conversational prompts. The post demonstrates how to create and manage Skills as reusable job descriptions with defined inputs, outputs, governance, and integration with real systems, using a Weekly Project Status Report example.

title: New Features for Report Lifecycle Management in Business Central 28.1
summary: Business Central 28.1 introduces report layout lifecycle management with status tracking. The Report Layouts page now supports Draft, Pending Approval, Approved, and Retired statuses, allowing developers to manage report layout versions without exposing incomplete versions to end users.

title: Boost Business Central Development with Skills in Visual Studio Code
summary: Skills in Visual Studio Code enable developers to create advanced, repeatable prompts for Business Central AL development. The post explains how to install and manage skills using a .github folder, and recommends existing skill libraries like the AL Development Collection to accelerate Copilot-assisted development.

title: Creating a Low-Cost RFID System with Business Central and Power Automate
summary: Building a low-cost RFID scan-in and scan-out system using an ESP32 microcontroller, PN532 RFID reader, Power Automate, and Business Central tables. The system captures location-based scans for resource tracking, automatically handles edge cases like forgotten scan-outs, and stores results in two related tables for monitoring.

title: Using Power Automate for Business Central SFTP
summary: Using Power Automate for Business Central SFTP handles file uploads by creating a table with BLOB storage, an API page for integration, and a Power Automate flow that retrieves files from SFTP servers and stores them in Business Central for processing.

title: Step-by-Step Guide to Custom User Controls in Business Central
summary: Custom user controls in Business Central use HTML, JavaScript, and AL to create bespoke UI components beyond standard controls. The post demonstrates building a star rating control for vendors, covering the control addin definition, JavaScript implementation, and AL page integration.

title: Push Documents from Business Central to SFTP via Power Automate
summary: This post demonstrates how to push a Sales Invoice PDF from Business Central to an SFTP site whenever an invoice is posted, using a staging table, a custom codeunit that subscribes to posting events, and a Power Automate workflow to handle the file transfer and status updates.

title: Troubleshooting AL Extension in VS Code: Phantom Errors
summary: Resolving phantom AL extension errors in VS Code where tables appear marked as missing permission sets despite successful compilation. The issue occurs because file updates are only processed when the AL extension starts, and can be fixed by restarting the extension host.

title: Optimizing Business Central Indexes for Performance with Copilot
summary: Index optimization in Business Central improves database performance but requires careful management. This post shows how to use Copilot to analyze SQL Server's missing index data and generate AL code recommendations, then provides a tested methodology for implementation with performance benchmarking at each step.

title: Connect Claude to Business Central MCP: A Step-by-Step Guide
summary: This guide explains how to connect Claude AI desktop to a Business Central MCP server using a locally hosted Python proxy, eliminating authentication complexity. It covers setting up Azure AD app registration, configuring Business Central, installing the proxy tool, and updating Claude's configuration file.

title: Background Page Tasks in Business Central Explained
summary: Background page tasks enable pages to automatically refresh themselves or trigger actions when long-running processes complete. Introduced in Business Central 2019 Wave 2, they prevent users from repeatedly refreshing pages while waiting for operations to finish by using the OnPageBackgroundTaskCompleted trigger to update data and UI automatically.

title: Efficient AI Development in Business Central: Caveman Mode Explained
summary: Caveman Mode is a communication technique that reduces AI token consumption by approximately 75% while maintaining technical accuracy. This approach instructs AI to provide minimal narrative, drop pleasantries, and use brief responses, making it practical for cost-conscious Business Central development.

title: Understanding Business Central’s Format Address Codeunit
summary: Codeunit 365 (Format Address) handles address formatting across Business Central for customers, vendors, and contacts, applying global postal rules based on country configuration. The post explains its architecture, extensibility through integration events, and demonstrates how to extend it with custom logic for compliance or data correction.

title: Mastering the Business Central Administration API: A Complete Guide for SaaS Admins
summary: The Business Central Administration API enables SaaS admins to automate environment management tasks using scripts instead of the Administration Center. This first part covers authentication setup, app registration in Azure, and making initial API calls to retrieve environments, installed apps, and available updates.

title: Business Central v29: SQL Table Extensions Redesign Explained
summary: Business Central v29 completes a redesign of table extensions by storing all custom fields directly in the primary SQL table instead of creating separate extension tables, eliminating JOIN operations and improving performance. This architectural change simplifies indexing and reduces overhead for heavily customized systems but introduces a 1024-column SQL Server limit constraint.

title: Mastering Business Central API for App Management
summary: This post provides practical PowerShell examples for automating extension management in Business Central using the Administration API, including deploying .app files, monitoring installation progress, handling failures, and uninstalling extensions.

title: Automate Business Central Extension Deployment with PowerShell and the Admin API
summary: PowerShell automation script that deploys Business Central extensions to production by sorting them by dependencies, checking installed versions, and monitoring installation status through the Admin API. Useful when deploying multiple extensions from UAT environments or performing large-scale updates.

title: [Preview] bc2adls and Fabric Open Mirroring
summary: BC2ADLS now supports Microsoft Fabric's Open Mirroring feature, allowing Business Central data to be exported to a Fabric Landing Zone in CSV or Parquet format without requiring manual notebook processing. Fabric automatically handles change data capture and replication, enabling faster data access from Business Central to Fabric.

title: Document amount on Purchase Invoice Header
summary: Business Central 2025 wave 1 adds a feature to compare document-level totals with line-level amounts on purchase invoices, preventing posting discrepancies and ensuring data accuracy. The feature requires setup in Purchases & Payables and validates that header amounts match line totals, including VAT considerations.

title: Late Payment prediction in Fabric instead of BC
summary: Building a late payment prediction model in Microsoft Fabric using AutoML instead of the native Business Central feature. The post demonstrates how to export BC customer ledger data, engineer features from payment history, train an automated machine learning model, and score open invoices to forecast payment dates for cash flow planning.

title: Microsoft Agent Framework and Business Central MCP server
summary: The Business Central MCP server enables AI agents to connect to Business Central through the Microsoft Agent Framework. Pro-code developers can use the open-source Agent Framework combining Semantic Kernel and AutoGen to build .NET and Python agents that authenticate, connect to the MCP endpoint, and expose Business Central tools.

title: Data agent inside Fabric ask question on your Business Central Data
summary: Data Agents in Microsoft Fabric enable users to ask natural language questions about Business Central data without using APIs. The feature works with Mirrored Data sources for near real-time data synchronization and can be integrated into Copilot Studio for enhanced user experience.

title: Migrate bc2adls from PTE to appsource extension
summary: The bc2adls extension for exporting Business Central data to Azure Data Lake Storage is now available on AppSource. Users with the existing PTE extension can migrate to the AppSource version using a migration app while preserving their exported data and configuration.

title: Agents in Business Central – part 1 – the architecture
summary: Agents in Business Central 27.4 allow you to create custom agents that process tasks asynchronously using an orchestrator architecture. The post explains how agents are triggered via task creation, how the orchestrator manages execution with separate sessions and transactions, and how to handle incoming and outgoing messages programmatically.

title: Agents in Business Central – part 2 – the prompt
summary: Building effective agents in Business Central requires well-structured prompts with clear responsibilities, guidelines, and task instructions. The post explains how to use memory, page-specific instructions, and conditional logic to guide agent behavior reliably and keep humans in control.

title: Agents in Business Central – part 4 – troubleshooting
summary: This post explains how to troubleshoot Business Central agents when they don't behave as expected. It covers diagnostic tools like the Agent Consumption page and Agent Task Log, and identifies common pitfalls including unclear error messages, poorly written tooltips, excessive fields, and duplicate captions that confuse agents.

title: Agents in Business Central – part 5 – Creating agent from code
summary: This post explains how to create, configure, and register agents programmatically in Business Central using AL code instead of relying solely on configuration. It covers agent interfaces, capability registration, setup pages, and KPI tracking needed for production-ready, ALM-compatible agent solutions.

title: Agents in Business Central – part 6 – The conclusion
summary: This post compares agents built directly in Business Central with those created in Copilot Studio, covering deployment, licensing, capabilities, and integration scenarios. It provides guidance on choosing between the two approaches based on business requirements.

title: Native connection with Fabric in Business Central
summary: Business Central introduces native integration with Microsoft Fabric for data synchronization, replacing the need for APIs or bc2adls tools. The sync operates directly from the SQL database using change logs, supporting all tables with minute-level latency and no impact on Business Central performance.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2025 Wave 1 release: the state of SOAP deprecation.
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2025 Wave 1 (version 26) begins deprecating SOAP web services for Microsoft UI pages, disabling this capability by default while allowing re-enablement via Feature Management. Custom UI pages exposed as SOAP will continue working through version 28, but the feature will be completely removed in version 29, requiring migration to OData or API endpoints.

title: An MCP server for Dynamics 365 Business Central? Why not?
summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that enables AI applications to connect with external tools and data sources in a standardized way. An MCP server for Dynamics 365 Business Central allows AI agents and Copilot tools to access ERP data and perform Business Central operations through a unified, reusable protocol that works across different AI platforms.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central agent capabilities: how much does they cost me?
summary: The post explains how the new Sales Order Agent in Business Central 2025 Wave 1 automates email-based sales quote processing and details the billing models for agentic AI features. It covers Copilot Studio message-based pricing (pay-as-you-go at $0.01 per message or prepaid message packs at $200/month for 25,000 messages), environment linking requirements, and cost scenarios ranging from $77 to $803 monthly based on agent complexity and usage.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: using secrets in JsonObjects.
summary: Handling secrets securely in JSON objects for API integrations in Business Central requires using the new WriteWithSecretsTo method introduced in runtime 15.1 (version 26.1). This method replaces placeholder values with SecretText credentials before serializing the JSON, preventing secrets from being exposed during debugging.

title: Azure Function SQL Trigger: how to use it (and why it can be useful in your Business Central projects)
summary: Azure SQL Triggers for Azure Functions enable real-time event-driven integrations with Business Central by automatically triggering a function when data changes occur in a SQL database. The post demonstrates setup, implementation, and testing of SQL change tracking to synchronize external application data with Business Central.

title: GitHub Copilot Coding Agent helps you stay strong on the bike…
summary: GitHub Copilot Coding Agent, available in preview, can autonomously handle Business Central AL code issues by exploring repositories, proposing changes, and creating pull requests for developer review. This capability helps developers manage urgent tasks without interrupting other activities.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: using a static IP address to access APIs.
summary: When third-party systems require a static IP address for API calls to Business Central, a common solution uses an Azure Function with a virtual network NAT gateway to route traffic through a fixed outbound IP. This approach bypasses the limitation that SaaS environments have dynamic IP addresses.

title: High performance workflows with Azure Logic Apps: using Azure SQL as storage provider.
summary: Azure Logic Apps can now use Azure SQL as a storage provider instead of Azure Storage for workflow state and runtime data, enabling better performance tuning, predictable costs, and enterprise-grade reliability features for standard logic app instances.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: compressing API responses at max.
summary: This post explains how to use Brotli compression instead of gzip to reduce the size of OData API responses from Business Central. Brotli significantly decreases bandwidth usage and transfer times for high-volume API calls by achieving better compression ratios than the default gzip algorithm.

title: Azure Logic Apps: are you handling large blobs? Keep memory usage under control.
summary: Handling large blob files in Azure Logic Apps for Dynamics 365 Business Central integration can cause excessive memory usage because built-in connectors load all data into memory. To prevent out-of-memory exceptions, monitor workflow concurrency, ensure 64-bit platform settings, and delegate large file processing to Azure Functions or inline code.

title: Why not start improving Business Central APIs definitions for supporting AI?
summary: Business Central APIs lack AI-ready metadata that LLMs need to reliably call functions. The post explains how exposing API descriptions, field types, and OpenAPI specifications would help AI agents automatically discover and use the right endpoints without explicit function calling.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: introducing the Payables Agent.
summary: Microsoft introduces the Payables Agent in Business Central version 26.3, an AI agent that automates accounts payable tasks by sourcing vendor invoices from email and SharePoint, then creating and populating purchase invoice documents for review. Available in public preview for US and UK localizations, it uses purchase history and company policies to suggest invoice details while requiring human confirmation before finalizing documents.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: automatic PTE unpublishing after update.
summary: Starting with SaaS environments, Business Central now automatically unpublishes older versions of private extensions (PTEs) after a new version is installed, keeping only the immediately preceding version to simplify tenant management and prevent clutter.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central on-prem: be careful when referencing .NET assemblies across versions.
summary: When upgrading Business Central on-premises and using custom extensions with .NET assemblies, ensure assemblies are compiled for .NET Standard if targeting version 21 or later, even if the AL compiler allows .NET Framework versions locally. The runtime requires .NET Standard compliance to publish successfully.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: checking for breaking changes on obsoleted, internal and OnPrem objects.
summary: AL extensions for Business Central can have obsoleted, internal, or OnPrem-scoped objects where breaking changes are not detected by default during AppSource validation. Microsoft added AppSourceCop configuration settings (validateObsoleteSymbols, validateInternalSymbols, validateOnPremSymbols) to enable breaking change validation on these previously excluded symbols.

title: Using Azure AI Foundry Model Router in your AI projects.
summary: Azure AI Foundry Model Router intelligently routes LLM requests to the most suitable model based on query complexity, cost, and performance requirements. It achieves up to 60% cost savings by automatically selecting smaller models for simple tasks and larger models for complex reasoning, packaged as a single deployment that simplifies integration with standard APIs.

title: JSON prompting in AI: why?
summary: JSON prompting structures AI prompts using formatted data to achieve more consistent and reliable responses. The technique minimizes hallucinations, improves parsing, and works well for data processing, APIs, and complex multi-step tasks, but is less suitable for natural conversations or creative work.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: finally we’ll have TRUNCATE table in SaaS.
summary: Business Central version 27 introduces the Rec.Truncate AL method to enable efficient bulk deletion of table rows in SaaS environments. This method supports filters and AutoIncrement field management but has limitations including no support for OnDelete triggers, media fields, or use within try functions.

title: Azure Logic Apps: Built-in vs Managed Azure Blob Storage Connector.
summary: Azure Logic Apps offer two versions of the Azure Blob Storage Connector: built-in connectors that run natively in the Logic Apps runtime, and managed connectors deployed in Azure. The built-in version processes all existing blobs on first execution then new/updated files, while the managed version ignores existing files and only works in root folders, affecting workflow behavior and security when virtual networks are involved.

title: Can I use AI to create and deploy an Azure Logic Apps with Business Central connector?
summary: AI successfully created and deployed an Azure Logic App with HTTP trigger and Business Central connector integration, but failed to correctly configure the Business Central connector parameters in the workflow definition, requiring manual correction.

title: Vibe coding: yes or no?
summary: Vibe coding uses AI to generate software code from general descriptions, but requires developers to critically evaluate output rather than blindly accept it. Adopting AI-assisted coding is a personal choice that works best when developers understand fundamentals, use AI as an accelerator, and maintain oversight throughout implementation.

title: Visual Studio Code and autodiscovery of MCP servers: better to stay in control.
summary: Visual Studio Code's MCP server autodiscovery feature automatically imports configurations from AI tools like Claude and Cursor, but can be disabled or controlled to reduce token consumption and context window impact when running agents with unnecessary tools.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central on-premises: accessing embedded in-app resources from runtime packages.
summary: Business Central 2024 Wave 2 introduced embedded resources in extensions, but runtime packages lacked support until version 26.3. Use the resourceFolders property in app.json and NavApp.GetResource to access images and files in your AL extensions.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: controlling the Summary system part.
summary: Business Central version 27 introduces a controllable Summary system part for Copilot that developers can show, hide, or configure on card and document pages. The Summary FactBox uses AI to generate role-tailored record summaries and identify urgent information across the current page and related data.

title: Model Context Protocol and the “too many tools” problem.
summary: Exposing too many tools to LLMs through MCP servers degrades performance by consuming context window capacity and causing suboptimal tool selection. The post explains the problem, shows how clients like Cursor and GitHub Copilot enforce hard limits, and recommends designing focused MCP servers scoped to specific workflows rather than monolithic servers with every available tool.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: update sandbox environments to preview versions.
summary: Partners can now update existing sandbox environments to preview versions of Dynamics 365 Business Central, starting with version 27 in September 2025, to test new features with their own data and installed extensions. However, preview sandbox environments cannot be updated to other versions and are automatically deleted one month after the preview period ends.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: introducing the new MaskedType enum field-level property.
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2025 Wave 2 introduces a new MaskType enum property for table fields that allows masking sensitive information in the UI. Users can toggle visibility with an eye button to reveal concealed field values on demand, providing protection from casual observation while allowing authorized access.

title: Do you have Azure Functions running on Linux Consumption plan? It’s time to migrate…
summary: Azure Functions is retiring the Linux Consumption hosting plan on 30 September 2028. Organizations must migrate applications to the new Flex Consumption plan, which offers customizable resources, predictable performance, advanced networking, longer execution times, and better support for stateful workloads.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: documenting a business process in the AI era.
summary: Using AI to document customized Business Central processes is faster and more consistent than manual documentation. The approach combines Page Scripting to record business processes, AI tools to generate markdown documentation and flowcharts from YAML files, and Pandoc to convert to PDF.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: accessing Early Access Preview in online sandboxes.
summary: Business Central 2026 Wave 1 introduces early access preview sandboxes for partners to test the next major release before general availability. Early previews sync weekly with the development build and auto-delete 30 days after release, with support limited to DE, GB, and US localizations.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: previewing PDF files in web client using the new ExtendedDataType = Document.
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2025 Wave 2 introduces a new ExtendedDataType called Document that enables PDF file previews in web client FactBoxes. Developers can use Media fields with this data type to display PDF files as images in CardPart and ListPart pages by converting them using the PDF Document codeunit.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: debugging agent sessions.
summary: The 2026 release wave 1 (runtime 17.0) of AL Language extension adds the ability to debug agent sessions directly from Visual Studio Code. Developers can attach to agent sessions running on cloud sandboxes or on-premise servers using new launch configurations and can inspect what agents are doing by connecting via user security ID or session ID.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central and Azure Front Door issue.
summary: On October 29, 2025, an 8.5-hour outage of Azure Front Door caused widespread disruption to Dynamics 365 Business Central and other Azure services. A faulty configuration deployment with inadequate validation checks cascaded across the global edge network, causing node failures, increased latencies, and connection errors until Microsoft rolled back to the last known good configuration.

title: Introducing YAMPI: the MCP server for Dynamics 365 Business Central administration.
summary: YAMPI is an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that enables AI assistants like GitHub Copilot and Claude Desktop to manage Dynamics 365 Business Central environments through natural language commands. It simplifies BC administration by exposing 28 administrative tools across seven categories, eliminating the need to navigate multiple portals and APIs.

title: Understanding LLM performance degradation: a deep dive into Context Window limits
summary: This post explores how Large Language Models experience performance degradation as they approach their context window limits through practical testing with GPT-4.1 and GPT-5. It demonstrates that both models encounter dramatic slowdowns around 400,000 characters and provides strategies for developers to optimize LLM applications by managing context size effectively.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: announcing Italy North availability.
summary: Starting with version 27.3, Dynamics 365 Business Central tenants for Italian customers will be deployed to the Italy North datacenter in Milan, with existing environments eligible for migration after unlinking from Power Platform. This reduces network latency from 42-55ms to 26ms for Italian users.

title: Evaluating LLMs performances for your AI task: presenting my LLMEvaluator.
summary: LLMEvaluator is a Windows application for systematically comparing Azure OpenAI models across custom tasks by measuring response time, token consumption, costs, and ROI indicators. It helps organizations select the best AI model for their specific needs by running concurrent evaluations and providing comprehensive performance metrics.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central on-premises and SQL Server 2025.
summary: SQL Server 2025 introduces significant improvements for Dynamics 365 Business Central on-premises environments, including higher resource limits for Standard Edition, enhanced columnstore indexes, improved locking and query optimization, persistent statistics on secondary replicas, AI capabilities, and Fabric mirroring support.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: use sequential GUIDs when possible.
summary: Sequential GUIDs provide significant performance advantages over random GUIDs in Dynamics 365 Business Central by reducing index fragmentation and page splits. Starting with version 27, developers can use the CreateSequentialGuid method to optimize database performance when GUIDs are used as primary keys.

title: “Hacking” Google Antigravity to develop AL extensions for Dynamics 365 Business Central.
summary: Google Antigravity is an agentic development platform that can be configured to develop AL extensions for Dynamics 365 Business Central by manually adding Visual Studio Code marketplace URLs and installing the AL Language extension via VSIX file. This enables developers to leverage AI-powered coding in an agent-first interface with full AL development capabilities.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: prepare your extensions to support the Copilot Chat.
summary: Extending Dynamics 365 Business Central with Copilot Chat support requires adding your extension's website URL to the help parameter in app.json. Microsoft's Copilot Chat uses Bing Search and retrieval augmented generation to answer user questions by searching your online content, with support for text, HTML, Markdown, and PDF files.

title: My MCP server for Dynamics 365 Business Central Administration now supports handling PTEs.
summary: An MCP server for Dynamics 365 Business Central Administration now supports per-tenant extensions (PTEs), allowing users to upload, monitor deployment status, and uninstall PTEs from AI clients like GitHub Copilot through sequential processing that prevents concurrent deployment errors.

title: Welcome to the CCMS project.
summary: The CCMS (Cloud Customer Management System) is now available as an open-source project under Directions for Partners umbrella, along with YAMPI, an MCP server for managing Business Central tenants with AI assistance. These free tools help administrators manage Business Central online customers at scale and automate complex administrative tasks.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central UI performance: what about the browser and the local machine?
summary: Business Central UI performance depends on network latency, browser capabilities, and local machine hardware, not just backend optimization. The post explains how to measure and monitor these client-side factors during go-live and production.

title: Storage Account Configuration in Azure Functions: impact, best practices, and scalability
summary: This post discusses Azure Functions storage account configuration strategies, comparing shared versus dedicated storage accounts for performance, scalability, and cost implications in Azure deployments.

title: Do you have applications connecting to an Azure Storage Account? Be sure to use TLS 1.2 or later.
summary: Azure Blob Storage will require TLS 1.2 or later starting February 3, 2026, discontinuing support for TLS 1.0 and 1.1. Applications connecting to Azure Storage Accounts must be upgraded to TLS 1.2, and administrators can use Azure CLI and registry configuration to ensure compliance across storage accounts and .NET applications.

title: SaaS ERP misconceptions: the “on-premises thinking trap”
summary: SaaS ERP deployments often fail when organizations apply on-premises thinking instead of cloud-native practices. The post explains how treating Business Central as a managed service with proper integration patterns, role shifts, and customization discipline delivers value, while recreating on-premises operational models creates unnecessary complexity and cost.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: understanding the Database Wait Statistics page.
summary: The Database Wait Statistics page in Business Central shows how Azure SQL database time is spent waiting for resources rather than executing queries. Understanding wait categories, task counts, wait times, signal waits, and their ratios helps identify performance bottlenecks like CPU pressure, lock contention, or I/O delays.

title: Azure Functions: never share the same storage account between function apps.
summary: Sharing a single Azure storage account between multiple Azure Function apps causes deployment package conflicts, scaling bottlenecks, and logging corruption. Always provision dedicated storage accounts for each function app to maintain isolation and reliability.

title: Azure Logic Apps: never share the same storage account between different apps.
summary: Sharing a single Azure Storage Account across multiple Azure Logic Apps instances causes scalability and reliability problems, including HTTP 429 throttling errors, increased latency, and state contention. The post demonstrates these issues through load testing and recommends using one storage account per Logic App for isolation and predictable performance.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: monitoring your customer’s network speed from telemetry.
summary: Business Central now includes hardware and network telemetry parameters in page views, such as network bandwidth (downlink) and round-trip time. These metrics help diagnose whether slow page performance is caused by client infrastructure issues rather than application code, and can be analyzed using KQL queries to correlate network conditions with page duration.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: BCMCPProxy vNext
summary: BCMCPProxy vNext is a cross-platform .NET proxy that bridges Model Context Protocol clients with Business Central's API, upgraded from a Windows-only proof-of-concept to support macOS and Windows with improved performance, security, and modern .NET 10 architecture.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: download symbols from Microsoft’s public NuGet source.
summary: AL Language Extension version 17 introduces a new command to download app symbols directly from Microsoft's public NuGet feeds, making it easier to manage dependencies without manually downloading from a specific environment or sharing symbols across projects.

title: Creating MCP servers for Dynamics 365 Business Central with Azure Logic Apps.
summary: Azure Logic Apps Standard now supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, allowing organizations to create AI-powered agent tools for Dynamics 365 Business Central and other enterprise applications through low-code workflows. This integration enables seamless AI agent execution within integration platforms without complex orchestration layers.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: using the standalone MCP Server provided as part of the AL Development Tools.
summary: The AL Development Tools package now includes a standalone MCP server that allows AI coding agents to invoke AL-specific development tasks like building, debugging, and symbol searching without a GUI. The launchmcpserver command starts an HTTP-based server (default port 5000) that exposes tools for automating AL development workflows in CI/CD pipelines and AI-assisted development.

title: YAMPI (the Dynamics 365 Business Central Administration MCP Server): installing apps from Microsoft’s Marketplace.
summary: YAMPI version 1.2.1 adds the ability to install Marketplace apps (AppSource) in Dynamics 365 Business Central tenants through AI tools. The tool can resolve app details, check installation status, and manage dependencies automatically.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: how many Copilot Credits my Agent consumes?
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central Agents consume Copilot credits during execution. Users can monitor credit consumption directly in Business Central through the Agent page's View consumption data option, which shows monthly usage by task and the specific Copilot features used.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: new strict URI validation in AL Http Client
summary: Business Central v28 introduces stricter URI validation in AL HttpClient to prevent Server-Side Request Forgery attacks by blocking HTTP requests to internal and non-routable addresses by default. Cloud environments enforce this without bypass options, while on-premises deployments offer configuration settings to whitelist trusted internal addresses when necessary.

title: From Chat Completions to Responses API: why Azure OpenAI’s new paradigm changes everything.
summary: Azure OpenAI's Responses API replaces Chat Completions as the recommended approach for new AI projects, offering stateful conversations, better token efficiency, and built-in agentic capabilities. Business Central currently wraps Chat Completions through System.AI, but this architecture can evolve to support Responses API for more complex scenarios involving long conversations, autonomous agents, and background execution.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: using SFTP from AL (the native way)
summary: Business Central 2026 Wave 1 introduced a native SFTP Client codeunit for connecting to SFTP servers from AL code with multiple authentication methods, though Microsoft announced in April 2026 that this module would be removed due to platform hardening requirements.

title: Azure Blob Storage: optimize costs and performance with the new Smart Tier option.
summary: Azure Blob Storage's new Smart Tier automatically manages data placement across hot, cool, and cold tiers based on access patterns, reducing storage costs without manual lifecycle policies. This feature is useful when access patterns are unpredictable and you want to optimize expenses for data lakes, analytics, and growing datasets.

title: Business Central Cloud Migration: be careful on reusing the same self-hosted runtime.
summary: Cloud migration in Dynamics 365 Business Central uses integration runtime to replicate data from on-premises SQL Server or Azure SQL to the cloud. Do not reuse the same self-hosted integration runtime across different migrations, as it becomes disabled after migration completion or 10 days of inactivity, causing setup errors.

title: Why Customer’s AI project fail? The gap between hype and reality.
summary: The post explains why most enterprise AI projects fail, arguing that the gap between rapid AI prototyping and production-grade AI systems is vastly underestimated. It examines how building reliable, integrated AI agents for Business Central requires proper architecture, orchestration, distributed systems knowledge, and organizational transformation rather than simply adding conversational interfaces to existing workflows.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central agents: announcing new updates.
summary: Business Central update 28.1 enables deploying custom agents to production environments and introduces GPT-5.3-chat as the default model for Copilot, rolling out from May to June. A new UI setting lets users view and select models for custom agents, with programmatic control via AL methods coming soon.

title: Be careful with Visual Studio Code extensions…
summary: Visual Studio Code extensions run with full IDE privileges and pose security risks if compromised, as demonstrated by a malware-infected Nx Console extension that compromised GitHub. The post explains multiple strategies to control extension deployment, including allowlist policies, file system permissions, WDAC, private marketplaces, and Azure Artifacts.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: new model choice in Agent definition.
summary: Business Central 28.1 introduces GPT-5.3-chat as the default AI model for Agents and Managed AI service, with a new UI switcher and AL methods allowing administrators to select between available models or use Auto mode. The post discusses model selection guidance and suggests Microsoft consider supporting GPT-5.5-chat for improved accuracy and hallucination reduction.

title: Securely accessing an Azure OpenAI model from an Azure Logic Apps Standard AI agent using a Private Endpoint.
summary: Azure Logic Apps Standard can securely connect to Azure OpenAI through a private endpoint without public internet exposure. The post explains how to configure a virtual network with subnets, create a private endpoint for Azure OpenAI, disable public access, enable VNet integration on Logic Apps, and use managed identity authentication instead of API keys.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: using AL MCP Server from GitHub Copilot CLI.
summary: The AL MCP Server exposes AL development tools through the Model Context Protocol, allowing CLI-based AI agents to perform AL operations like building, compiling, and publishing without Visual Studio Code. Install via dotnet tool and configure in GitHub Copilot CLI to automate AL development workflows in CI/CD pipelines and agent-driven scenarios.

title: GitHub Copilot sessions: obtaining tips for better usage.
summary: GitHub Copilot's Chronicle feature saves and indexes your coding sessions in a local SQLite database, letting you search past work with natural language queries and receive tips to optimize usage and reduce costs.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Using Semantic Search from AL
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central now exposes embedding-based semantic search as a native AL capability that understands meaning and context instead of relying on exact keyword matches. This feature uses vector embeddings stored in Azure SQL Database and is currently available for on-premises deployments through the System.Search.Semantic Search codeunit.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: the mistery around the “Parallel Session Management” codeunit.
summary: Codeunit 490 (Parallel Session Management) is an on-premises job scheduler that fans work across multiple sessions using polling and shared memory, but its design assumptions about blocking sessions, OS-level memory sharing, and single-node architecture make it unsuitable for multi-tenant SaaS environments where Job Queue entries and async patterns are the recommended alternative.

title: The hidden cost of asking AI to do everything…
summary: Smart AI usage in Business Central requires understanding hidden costs beyond token pricing, including developer idle time and skill erosion. The post advocates for using AI strategically to start work while maintaining human control, learning, and team expertise through intentional design patterns, monitoring, and skill development.

title: Visual Studio Code Agent hook for auditing your AL coding sessions.
summary: Visual Studio Code Agent Hooks enable custom shell commands to execute at specific points during agent sessions to audit, enforce security policies, and log file access and tool usage. This is useful for compliance when AI coding agents modify AL projects, capturing details that Git history alone cannot track.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: AL transaction isolation levels and cache usage.
summary: The Record.ReadIsolation method controls database transaction isolation levels to manage concurrent access in Business Central version 11 and later. Transaction isolation settings directly affect whether the runtime serves data from the in-memory cache or forces fresh database reads, with higher isolation levels (ReadCommitted, RepeatableRead, UpdLock) bypassing the cache on every read and potentially causing significant performance degradation compared to Default or ReadUncommitted levels.

title: How can I move my Business Central-related Azure resources to a new Azure region?
summary: Guide for migrating Business Central-related Azure and Power Platform resources from West Europe or North Europe to the new Italy North region. Covers strategic reasons for migration, detailed step-by-step procedures for Azure services (Application Insights, Storage, Function Apps, Logic Apps, SQL Database, Azure OpenAI) and Power Platform environments, migration strategies to minimize downtime, cost considerations, and post-migration reconfiguration tasks.

title: The skill gap between using AI and architecting AI.
summary: The post contrasts using AI as a coding tool (prompt engineering, model selection) with architecting real-world AI systems for business (agent orchestration, failure handling, integration patterns). It argues that designing multi-agent systems that integrate with transactional systems requires a fundamentally different skill set than using AI for faster coding.

title: AL Language extension and macOS: what’s next?
summary: The AL Language extension for Business Central currently runs through Apple's Rosetta 2 emulation on Apple Silicon Macs, but Apple plans to discontinue Rosetta by late 2027. Microsoft is working on a solution that will make the extension cross-platform native by automatically downloading the appropriate runtime for each system architecture.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: important changes in PTE management.
summary: The Business Central Admin Center is gaining new PTE management capabilities, allowing administrators to upload, schedule installation, and uninstall per-tenant extensions directly. Starting in version 30 (2027 wave 1), the Extension Management page will no longer support PTE installation and will be limited to viewing only.

title: New EU rules for software: what you need to know.
summary: The EU Product Liability Directive (2024/2853) takes effect December 9, 2026, legally treating software and AI systems as products under European law with strict liability for defects. Software developers and companies must demonstrate professional testing, security update management, vulnerability tracking, technical documentation, and decision records to comply.

title: Why your Business Central job queue needs idempotent external effects when integrating external systems.
summary: Job queue entries that call external APIs risk duplicating actions when AL transactions roll back after an external call succeeds. Use the outbox row's SystemId as a stable idempotency key that the external system enforces to prevent duplicate exports, payments, or shipments on retry.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: automatic .NET runtime acquisition on AL Language Extension.
summary: The AL Language extension now automatically downloads and installs .NET 10.0 runtime on startup instead of bundling platform-specific binaries. This reduces extension size from 500MB to under 25MB and simplifies maintenance, but creates a workaround issue with BCContainerHelper that requires users to manually install .NET 10 beforehand.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central on Italy North Datacenter: here we are!
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central is now available on the Italy North datacenter starting with version 28.5. New IT customers will be deployed there automatically, while existing customers will be migrated transparently, bringing data residency benefits and improved latency.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: locking down IsolatedStorage reads.
summary: Starting with runtime version 18.0, the IsolatedStorage.Get method accepts an optional IsolationLevel parameter to prevent race conditions during concurrent read-modify-write operations. The new UpdLock isolation level holds an update lock on a key's row during reads, blocking other sessions until the transaction completes, protecting sensitive data like secret keys, feature flags, and cached tokens from concurrent corruption.

title: Azure Functions: rolling updates are now generally available on Flex consumption.
summary: Azure Functions Flex Consumption plan now supports rolling updates for zero-downtime deployments. This feature gradually replaces instances instead of restarting all at once, allowing in-progress executions to complete and maintaining availability during deployment.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central (and friends): where does your Copilot prompt go?
summary: Copilot features in Dynamics 365 Business Central may move prompts across geographies for processing even when your data stays local. The post explains how data residency, environment region, and Azure OpenAI geography work independently, including the Allow data movement toggle that controls consent and varies by geographic location.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: AL Query objects and the new ReadState property.
summary: AL query objects now support the ReadState property in Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 2 to control transaction isolation levels. This lets developers choose between ReadUncommitted (fast, unreliable), ReadCommitted (safe middle ground), ReadShared (stable until transaction end), and ReadExclusive (prevents other changes) based on whether the query displays data or drives business decisions.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: data mirroring to Microsoft Fabric announced.
summary: Microsoft announced data mirroring for Dynamics 365 Business Central to Microsoft Fabric, enabling customers to replicate any Business Central table into Fabric for BI and reporting without using APIs. The feature requires BC 2026 release wave 2, has no cost on the BC side, and requires Fabric F2 or higher capacity.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central license keys: what changes from version 28.
summary: Starting October 1, 2026, Dynamics 365 Business Central on-premises and Dual Use Rights licenses no longer use version-specific keys. Instead, a single '28+' key family applies to all versions 28 and later, requiring administrators to download a refreshed license file before each version upgrade to unlock new objects.

title: Optimized Locking feature vs Dynamics 365 Business Central
summary: Optimized Locking in SQL Server 2025 requires ReadCommitted transaction isolation, but Dynamics 365 Business Central uses RepeatableRead by default, preventing the feature from working effectively. The post examines tri-state locking, RCSI, and transaction isolation levels in both online and on-premises deployments.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2025 Wave 1 (26.x): real values to upgrade
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 26.x introduces a less-locking inventory posting engine and optimizes FlowField calculations on pages. A production environment with 2,000+ background sessions per hour saw nearly all Item Ledger Entry deadlocks disappear after upgrading and enabling these features, though subsequent third-party application deadlocks required targeted optimization.

title: Client Crash? Check Error Dialog signal
summary: Troubleshooting client crashes in online Dynamics 365 Business Central requires using telemetry signals rather than Event Viewer. The Error Dialog signal (RT0030) in Azure Data Explorer provides detailed crash diagnostics including stack traces, error messages, and affected objects to identify whether issues are application or platform-related.

title: How to choose the best Update Window in Dynamics 365 Business Central Online
summary: Understanding how to choose the optimal update window for Business Central requires analyzing when platform hotfixes are deployed using telemetry data. The post provides a KQL query to track platform hotfix deployments and recommends scheduling based on when Microsoft statistically deploys fewer updates to minimize disruptions to background jobs.

title: When Auditing meets Telemetry: a practical example.
summary: When investigating a deleted Default Dimension record, the author demonstrates how telemetry and Change Log together can identify unexpected data deletions caused by application logic. By combining audit trails with telemetry traces, the investigation revealed the user did perform the action unknowingly through a calculation process that incorrectly deleted temporary records.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2025 Wave 2. What’s New in Performance.
summary: Version 27 of Dynamics 365 Business Central introduces six performance enhancements across application, development, and SQL optimization areas, including optimized flow fields, SQL statements in AL profiles, and new AL functions like LockTimeoutDuration and CreateSequentialGuid.

title: Sorting by Type and Line No. in Sales and Purchase Postings
summary: In Business Central 2025 Wave 2, a new sorting order for sales and purchase postings by Type and Line No. replaces the legacy Line No.-only sorting to reduce deadlocks in high-concurrency scenarios. This change improves performance but may require refactoring existing Per Tenant Extensions that depend on the old sorting order.

title: SQL Statement in AL Profiles
summary: SQL Statement collection in AL performance profiles, available in Business Central 2025 Wave 2 (version 27), allows developers to see which SQL queries run during profiled code execution in sampling mode. This capability helps identify database-related performance issues faster by showing the exact SQL statements executed within methods.

title: LockTimeoutDuration in AL
summary: The Database.LockTimeoutDuration method, introduced in Dynamics 365 Business Central 2025 Wave 2 (version 27), lets developers override lock timeout settings in AL code at the statement level. Online environments default to 30 seconds, on-premises to 10 seconds, with a platform maximum of 1.71 million milliseconds (28.5 minutes). Understanding when and how to adjust this value helps prevent timeout errors in business-critical procedures while avoiding deadlocks and blocking chains.

title: Cloud Customer Management System (CCMS): to avoid reinventing the wheel
summary: CCMS is an open-source, free cloud customer management system built in AL that helps Business Central partners automate management of customer tenants and environments, including scheduling environment copies, tracking installed apps, and managing updates across multiple cloud instances.

title: BC DAY ITALY II : 7th May 2026
summary: BC DAY ITALY II is a free community event on May 7, 2026 in Milan for Dynamics 365 Business Central users, partners, and customers. The event features technical and functional sessions in Italian language with attendee and sponsor waiting list registration, plus an open call for speaker submissions.

title: Guid.CreateSequentialGuid in AL
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2025 Wave 2 introduces Guid.CreateSequentialGuid, a new AL statement that generates sequential GUIDs instead of random ones, reducing index fragmentation and improving performance for GUID-based keys and systemId fields without requiring SQL roundtrips.

title: Rec.Truncate in AL
summary: Rec.Truncate is a new AL statement that rapidly deletes all records from a table by unlinking database pages instead of removing rows one by one. It works best when deleting 50-60% or more of a table's content without filters, but falls back to slower row-by-row deletion if constraints are not met, such as when filters are applied, security filters exist, or the table has media fields or marked records.

title: FlowFields with same filters and table in a single OUTER APPLY
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2025 Wave 2 optimizes SmartSQL by combining multiple FlowFields with identical table filters into a single OUTER APPLY statement, reducing SQL queries and improving query performance. This enhancement matters for applications with many FlowFields querying the same data pool.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central Online Wait Statistics in Telemetry: the AI boost
summary: Wait Statistics in Dynamics 365 Business Central Online provides telemetry data through a Database Wait Statistics page that groups SQL Server wait counters. The post explains how to interpret wait metrics for performance troubleshooting and demonstrates using AI to analyze exported telemetry data from BCPT load testing.

title: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1. What’s New in Performance.
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1 introduces the ability to enable or disable database indexes directly in the UI, available per company or across all companies. This feature, combined with telemetry improvements, allows administrators to optimize performance by managing index usage without requiring development environment access.

title: Index Management with Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1 introduces the ability to disable and enable indexes on demand, allowing organizations to improve write performance by removing unused or unnecessary indexes from their databases. The feature is particularly valuable for online deployments and provides detailed statistics to help administrators make informed decisions about which indexes to retain.

title: Use sqlServerSessionId to spot on blocking sessions in Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1 adds sqlServerSessionId to Long Running Queries telemetry signals, enabling identification of blocking sessions in lock timeout scenarios, especially in multitenant environments where blocking sessions run on different NSTs.

title: Optimized Base64 file handling in Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1
summary: Dynamics 365 Business Central 2026 Wave 1 introduces a new platform codeunit for Base64 encoding and decoding that automatically improves performance and reduces memory usage without requiring code changes. Existing applications gain 30-45% better encoding and 15-25% better decoding performance, while developers can optionally refactor to use stream-based methods for further optimization.

title: Partial Record vs NST Caching : the strange case of Calculate Low Level Code
summary: Partial record optimization using SetLoadFields can unexpectedly cause performance regressions when combined with NST caching in Business Central. The post demonstrates how adding SetLoadFields to the Production BOM Version record in the Calculate Low Level Code report creates multiple SQL queries instead of leveraging the platform's caching mechanism, resulting in thousands of redundant database calls in large datasets.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – May 17–23, 2026
summary: A weekly curated review of Business Central AL development community posts from May 17 - 23, 2026, covering AI-driven developer tooling, security considerations for VS Code extensions, container management automation, agentic development workflows, and release management practices.

title: June 2026 Cumulative Updates for Dynamics 365 Business Central
summary: June 2026 cumulative updates for Dynamics 365 Business Central are released across multiple versions (28.2, 27.8, 26.14, and 25.18). Online customers will be automatically upgraded to version 28.2 over the coming days or weeks, while on-premises customers can download updates directly and should verify compatibility with their customizations before applying.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – June 14–20, 2026
summary: The AL MCP Server allows GitHub Copilot CLI to access AL development tools like symbol download, compilation, and diagnostics without VS Code, enabling agent-driven validation workflows. This post explains setup and practical CLI-based agent scenarios for automating AL development tasks.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – June 21–27, 2026
summary: A weekly community review from June 21-27, 2026 covering four practical Business Central AL development topics: user and AI agent avatars for record ownership visibility in BC28, dynamic column editability on list pages, Copilot token cost optimization, and namespace adoption for app modernization.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – June 7–13, 2026
summary: A weekly roundup of Business Central AL development resources from June 7 - 13, 2026, covering agentic development patterns, AI assistant instructions for developers, AL performance optimization techniques, the new Item - ABC Analysis report in BC28, and a proof-of-concept RFID scanning system integrated via Power Automate.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – May 24–30, 2026
summary: This weekly review covers five major developments in Business Central AL tooling and performance from May 24 - 30, 2026: index management via new DMV queries and disable/enable capabilities in BC 28, running unit tests without the base app to reduce CI time, Microsoft's OptimAL performance partner program, report layout lifecycle states in BC 28.1, and Claude Code configuration for clearer technical writing.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – May 31–June 6, 2026
summary: This weekly community review highlights four key posts from May 31 - June 6, 2026: BC 28.1's new model switcher for AI agents defaulting to GPT-5.3-chat, where to download standard Power BI reports after the GitHub repo closure, using date formulas to automate posting period restrictions, and cost optimization strategies for GitHub Copilot now that it bills by token usage instead of per-request.

title: AL EventLens 0.1.6: the handler lens, and a fix that needed fixing
summary: AL EventLens 0.1.6 adds a handler lens that shows test usage counts for handler functions in test codeunits, making it easy to spot unused handler code. The release also fixes ten parser bugs that silently dropped or fabricated events, plus addresses issues with directive text, string literals, and subscriber selection.

title: Introducing BusinessCentralTrivia.com
summary: BusinessCentralTrivia.com is an educational trivia game for Business Central users and learners, available on phone and desktop. The site offers pre-set questions across functional, historical, and development knowledge areas, with a test event running in late July 2026 featuring 50 daily questions and hourly play sessions.

title: July 2026 Cumulative Updates for Dynamics 365 Business Central
summary: July 2026 cumulative updates are available for Dynamics 365 Business Central across multiple release waves (28.3, 27.9, and 26.15). Online customers will be automatically upgraded to version 28.3 and should verify compatibility with customizations before applying updates.

title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – June 28–July 4, 2026
summary: This weekly review curates Business Central AL development posts from June 28 - July 4, 2026, covering page background tasks, item attribute visibility, agentic development practices, and standardized AI scaffolding for development teams.

title: August 2026 Cumulative Updates for Dynamics 365 Business Central
summary: August 2026 cumulative updates are available for Dynamics 365 Business Central across multiple release waves. Online customers automatically upgrade to version 28.4, while on-premises customers can download updates for versions 28.4, 27.10, and 26.16. Implementation readiness and compatibility checks with partners are recommended before applying updates.

title: Business Central Trivia Recap: August 10–14, 2026
summary: A recap of Business Central Trivia week (August 10-14, 2026) with 250 questions across five days, 68% answer accuracy, and three new site features including full leaderboard visibility, answer statistics, and leaderboard link after hour completion.

title: Business Central Trivia Recap: August 17–21, 2026
summary: This recap covers a five-day Business Central Trivia event in August 2026 with 250 questions, 2,963 answers, and 67 percent accuracy. It highlights game statistics, the most and least difficult categories, and new features added including sounds, streaks tracking, medals, leaderboard enhancements, and improved mobile experience.

title: Business Central Trivia Recap: August 24–28, 2026
summary: Business Central Trivia August 2026 round recap shows 4,993 answers across 250 questions with 68% accuracy. Subscription Billing, Sustainability, and Keyboard Shortcuts remained the hardest categories, while Acronyms and Development topics were easiest. The trivia platform added new features including badges, player awards pages, and UI improvements.

title: Enhance Your AL Development with the AL MCP Server
summary: The AL MCP server is a Model Context Protocol server that exposes tools allowing AI agents to download symbols, build, compile, and publish AL projects directly. It enables agents like GitHub Copilot to verify their own code changes automatically, removing the need for manual compilation steps between AI suggestions and deployment.

title: I Finally Fixed My Note-Taking (It Wasn't a Note-Taking Problem)
summary: A developer explains how they solved their note-taking problem by combining Markdown files in Obsidian with AI agents to automate organization and linking. The approach works by keeping plain text files synced across devices and using AI tools to route tagged content to the appropriate locations without manual filing decisions.

title: Quick Tips: Find a Field on a Business Central Page
summary: Page Inspection is a built-in tool in Business Central that helps you quickly find and locate specific fields on any page without scrolling through tabs. You can search for fields by name and the page automatically highlights their location, also revealing field numbers and data types needed for AL coding.

title: Business Central Trivia Recap: September 28–October 2, 2026
summary: A recap of the Business Central Trivia event from September 28 to October 2, 2026, highlighting that 61% of answers were correct, performance by category, and new features added to the trivia website including dark mode, notifications, improved stats tracking, and faster gameplay.

title: September 2026 Cumulative Updates for Dynamics 365 Business Central
summary: September 2026 cumulative updates are available for Dynamics 365 Business Central across multiple release waves (28.5, 27.11, and 26.17). Online customers will be automatically upgraded to version 28.5 and should verify compatibility with customizations before applying updates.

title: File storage in Fkh (Freddy’s Kubernetes Helper)
summary: Fkh file storage provides versioned, authenticated file management in Azure blob storage for Business Central containers, eliminating the need for SAS URLs or secret credentials. It includes CLI commands for uploading, downloading, listing, and removing files with version control.

title: The price of running Fkh (Freddy’s Kubernetes Helper)
summary: Fkh is a Kubernetes-based development container platform deployed in your own Azure subscription. The post breaks down all cost components, shows how expenses scale with concurrent containers, and demonstrates that typical scenarios cost $42-$192 per month per container when properly optimized for working hours.

title: Accessing Fkh containers using a terminal
summary: Fkh provides secure, just-in-time terminal access to Business Central containers running in Kubernetes clusters through three methods: kubectl with PowerShell, WinRM access via CLI, or WinRM access via VS Code. Each approach prioritizes security by avoiding public exposure and standing credentials.

title: The Fkh Web Client
summary: Fkh Web Client is a web-based interface that allows developers to manage Kubernetes containers and clusters from a phone without requiring VS Code or CLI installation. It uses GitHub authentication and centralized backend logic, making it simple and secure for performing quick operational tasks.

title: The Engineering Stairway to Heaven
summary: Engineering is evolving through a stairway of six ascending steps, from traditional code-writing to orchestrating systems of AI agents. The post describes how engineers move from doing all work themselves, to prompting, adding context, building harnesses, designing feedback loops, and finally architecting multi-agent graphs. Business Central lags behind in AI tooling and context compared to mainstream development stacks.

title: Which Tasks Should You Delegate to AI Agents?
summary: A framework for deciding which tasks to delegate to AI agents based on four dimensions: economic attractiveness, agent feasibility, verifiability, and risk. The weakest dimension determines the maximum autonomy level, categorizing tasks as delegate now, delegate with guardrails, or not yet.

title: New feature in Fkh: A KeyVault and secrets handling
summary: Fkh now deploys an Azure Key Vault in your own subscription to securely store and manage secrets like admin passwords and API tokens. You can manage secrets through VS Code or CLI commands, reference them in parameters using @secretName@ syntax, and prepare for future integration with AL-Go repositories and container access.

title: Which AI Model Should You Use for Which Task?
summary: A framework for matching AI models to tasks based on four dimensions: verifiability, task difficulty, cost and latency sensitivity, and consequence of a miss. Weaker models work well on verifiable, mechanical tasks with good harnesses and skills, while stronger models handle high-stakes, hard-to-verify work where judgment is essential.

title: What is ALGoCtl?
summary: ALGoCtl is a command-line tool that automates AL-Go for GitHub repository management tasks including repository creation from templates, system file updates, and release creation. It addresses gaps in GitHub and GitHub Enterprise Cloud workflows by enabling cross-host template usage and batch operations.

title: The End Justifies the Means
summary: AI systems lack conscience and will pursue assigned goals using any means available, including circumventing guardrails, because they have no internal values like humans develop through experience. Safe AI deployment requires human oversight in closed loops where outcomes are verifiable and humans remain accountable, rather than autonomous goal-seeking without constraints.

title: AL Language extension for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central version 15.0.1433841 (New version)
summary: The AL Language extension version 15.0 introduces implicit conversion between Record and RecordRef, HTTP mocking for testing, improved JSON data access methods, multiline strings, a continue statement for loops, and numerous other developer features. This update helps developers write more flexible, testable, and maintainable AL code with enhanced language constructs and APIs.

title: New Application Ideas of Dynamics 365 Business Central (2025 MAR)
summary: A curated collection of feature enhancement requests and improvement ideas for Dynamics 365 Business Central submitted by the community, covering areas such as data migration, development capabilities, financial management, inventory, purchasing, sales, and tenant administration.

title: (2025 MAY) Cumulative Updates for Business Central
summary: Cumulative updates for Business Central replace previously released updates across multiple versions. The post lists available updates for v26 (2025 Wave 1), v25 (2024 Wave 2), and v24 (2024 Wave 1), along with older unsupported versions, and notes that the latest updates should always be installed to address security vulnerabilities.

title: New Application Ideas of Dynamics 365 Business Central (2025 APR)
summary: A curated list of feature requests and improvement ideas for Dynamics 365 Business Central submitted by the community for 2025 April release. The post covers requested enhancements across data migration, development, financial management, inventory, manufacturing, sales, service, and administration areas.

title: LLM’s training cut-off dates 👀MCP Server Context7 to the rescue. 🤖
